summary: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Elphinstone College, Deccan College, and Government Law College, Mumbai. He taught at New English School (~1880–1885) and Fergusson College (~1885–1890).

Bal Krishen Thapar worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying at the University of the Punjab, under Mortimer Wheeler at Taxila, and at Heidelberg. He was Director General of Archaeology (1978–1981) and chaired the CCRT (1982–1992).
Bala Sahai Shastri was an Indologist who served at Panjab University as Assistant to the Librarian (attested 1932) and in-charge of the Sanskrit Section (attested 1947).
Bangwei Wang is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He completed his doctoral studies at Peking University (~1983–1987) and became a professor there in ~1992.

Banikanta Kakati worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Cotton University, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta. He served as a professor at Cotton University (1918–1947) and became Dean and department head at Gauhati University in 1948.

Bapudeva Sastri was an Indology scholar who studied at Sehore High School under Lancelot Wilkinson, Dhundiraja Misra, and Sevarama. He taught at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi (Sampurnanand Sanskrit University) from 1842 to 1889.

Barbara E. Ward was a Sinology scholar who studied at Newnham College, the University of London, and LSE. Her posts included teaching history at the University of London (~1956–1965) and lecturing at the University of Cambridge (~1973–1978).

Barbara Gerke is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar who earned a D.Phil. at Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel. She held research posts at Berlin (2011–2015), Oxford (attested 2017), and Vienna (attested 2022).

Barbara Mittler is a Sinology and history/archaeology scholar. She studied at Pearson College, the Mandarin Training Center, Oxford (~1987–1990), and the University of Heidelberg (~1990–1994), holding a post at Heidelberg in 1993.

Barbara Nimri Aziz is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. She completed her B.A. at Queen's University and her Ph.D. under Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf at SOAS (1969–1974), later holding a post at the University of Oran in 2007.

Indologist Barbara Stoler Miller studied at Barnard College, Columbia, and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown and Stella Kramrisch. She had a long career at Barnard College and Columbia University (~1968–1993).

Barbra R. Clayton works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University (attested 2001) under Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, and held a post at Mount Allison University (attested 2013).
Barend Faddegon was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Amsterdam and served as a professor there from 1907 to 1944.

Sinologist and historian Barend J. ter Haar studied under Erik Zürcher and Susan Naquin at Leiden University (PhD ~1984–1990). He held posts at Heidelberg (~1994–2000) and as a professor at Leiden University (~2000–2013).

Barend Jan Terwiel works in history, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Utrecht and the Australian National University, and held professorships at the University of Munich (~1991–1992), Hamburg (1992–2007), and Leiden (1999–2004).
Barnabé Brisson studied at the College of Juilly, École polytechnique (1794–1796), and École des Ponts ParisTech (1796–1798), later holding a post at École des Ponts ParisTech from 1820 to 1824.

Barry Kerzin works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at UC Berkeley, USC, and under Geshe Namgyal Wangchen. He taught medicine at the University of Washington (1985–1989) and was an honorary and adjunct professor at the University of Hong Kong.

Barry Sautman specializes in Sinology and Tibetology. Educated at UCLA, NYU, and Columbia, he held posts at California State University, Northridge (1990–1991), and served as assistant professor at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (1993–2008).
Bart Dessein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy who studied under Charles Willemen. He served as an Associate Professor at Ghent University (attested 2014–2019).

Linguist Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve studied at Princeton, Bonn, and Göttingen under Friedrich Ritschl and Friedrich Wilhelm Schneidewin. He was Professor of Greek at the University of Virginia (1856–1876) and a professor at Johns Hopkins University (1876–1915).
